item.subject: maths
item.stem:
Lalit looks at the diagram of a library shelf-number grid. Each entry increases by $1$ across a row and by $8$ down a column. He claims that in any $2\times 2$ block the two diagonal sums are equal, for every such block.

Which plan correctly proves that the relation always holds?

options.A: Let the top-left entry be $n$. The block is $n$, $n+1$, $n+8$, $n+9$; both diagonals equal $2n+9$, so the relation holds for every $n$.
options.B: Check three sample blocks and stop, skipping a letter-number reference entry with the fixed $+1$ and $+8$ offsets.
options.C: Treat the equal diagonal sums as deciding which number must sit in the top-left cell, instead of proving the sums from a chosen reference entry.
options.D: Use the same letter-number offsets to place beads on a cyclic design circle, beyond proving a shelf-grid relation.
